compiled_state.description:
## Problem

The config-root guard flags `os.path.dirname(tracker)` but **does NOT flag** `os.path.dirname(StorePaths(tracker).canonical)`. Both compose the repo/config root from the store path — the precise construct the guard exists to eliminate — but only the first is detected.

Measured on 2026-08-28 while adjudicating `scathing-custommade-bobcat` (6bf1-326b-7404-4034): both forms were placed in one file under `src/`; the guard flagged the bare form and passed the `.canonical` form.

## Why this matters more than a missed lint

The guard is what makes an acceptance criterion like 6bf1 AC#3 ("ZERO deferred config-root sites") meaningful. A construct the guard cannot see would sit in the tree **unflagged**, while that AC truthfully reports zero — so the criterion would pass while the defect class it protects is present. A guard with a blind spot is worse than a missing guard, because it converts an unchecked assumption into a checked-looking one.

This is not hypothetical: a concurrently-proposed redesign of `run_sweep` used exactly `dirname(canonical tracker)` as its fallback arm and would have entered the tree unsanctioned.

## Mechanism

By its own docstring the detector matches the bare name, `*.tracker_dir()`, and `str()`-wrapped forms, and deliberately does **not** unwrap the `realpath`/`abspath` family. `StorePaths(...).canonical` is in that unwrapped family. The guard remedy text already names `config.repo_root_or_none()` as the sanctioned fix, so the intended contract is clear; the detector simply does not cover this spelling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The guard flags `os.path.dirname(StorePaths(tracker).canonical)` in a file under `src/`.
- [ ] The guard flags the equivalent `realpath`/`abspath`-wrapped spellings of the same composition, or the decision to exclude each is recorded in the guard docstring with its reason.
- [ ] No existing sanctioned site newly fails: the guard still exits 0 on the current tree, or every new finding is triaged and either fixed or sanctioned.
- [ ] The detector change is proven non-vacuous: a seeded positive is flagged AND the clean tree passes, so the test cannot pass by never running.

## Testing

- Add a guard self-test that seeds each newly-covered spelling and asserts a finding, plus a negative control asserting the clean tree passes.
- Mutation-check: disable the new matching arm and confirm the seeded case survives (proving the assertion is load-bearing). Verify the seed actually applied — anchor the edit to a line start, since a replace that lands in a comment produces a mutant that was never seeded.
- Run the full guard over the repo and record the before/after finding counts.
compiled_state.title: Config-root guard misses dirname(StorePaths(tracker).canonical), the exact construct it exists to catch
